# aeneid-003 — review (I.198–296)

Adversarial review in two passes. Pass 1: every unit, field by field (`n` labels against the form in its line,
Latin → `l` word by word, `l` ↔ `i`, remembered English in `i`/`l`, speech marks, factual claims in `n` and
`about`), plus a hand scansion of all 99 lines set against the scanner's output (every long syllable tested for
nature or position, every short one tested for nature, then every word with Ae-, Greek vowels, consonantal i,
hiatus, synizesis). Pass 2: re-read of the edited file; one more change (#23 `n`); every one of the 99 lines
re-checked by script as six valid feet after `scan-fixes.json` is applied. All edits to `units.json` were made by
script; `t`, `ln`, `p`, `v` are unchanged (checked against the file as received); speech marks in `l`/`i` agree
with `t` on every unit (opens: #0, #19, #31; closes: #8, #29, #51).

**Counts:** Major 5 · Medium 20 · Low 15 · scan fixes added 10 · refused/verified-and-kept 19.
Changed: 5 `l`, 18 `i`, 17 `n` (27 units) and `about`.

Remembered English: the version the draft kept echoing is Fairclough's Loeb prose (1916). It is public domain,
but the rule is the same for every known version: distinctive overlaps were rephrased. The check was made from
memory, not by collation.

## Major (false label or broken `l`)

1. **#24 (I.242–246) `l` and `i`** — the `l` moved `tutus` (end of 243) onto the line of `regna Liburnorum`, so the
   `l` line division no longer matched `t`. Now "…and the inmost, safe," / "realms of the Liburnians, and the
   spring…". The `i` also turned `penetrare` into "make his way past"; `penetrare` governs both `sinus` and
   `intima regna` ("enter, thread"). Now "could thread the Illyrian gulfs and, safe, the inmost realms…".
2. **#34 (I.260) `l`, `i`, `n`** — "nor me has my purpose turned" and "nor has my resolve turned me" made Jupiter's
   own purpose the subject of the turning. Venus asked *quae te sententia vertit*; he answers that no purpose
   has turned him. Now `l` "nor me has any purpose turned", `i` "and no change of mind has turned me", note rewritten.
3. **#32 (I.257–258) `n`** — `tuorum` called "the genitive plural of `tui`". It is the genitive plural of `tuus`
   (`tui` is the genitive of the pronoun `tu`). Fixed.
4. **#25 (I.247–249) `n`** — `Teucrorum` labelled "an old genitive plural". It is the ordinary `-orum` genitive plural
   (the old forms are the `-um` ones). Fixed, with `sedes` as its head.
5. **#4 (I.203) `l`** — "perhaps even this" rendered `haec`, which is neuter plural (and the note said so). Now
   "perhaps even these things, some day, it will please to remember". `new-renderings.md` updated to match.

## Medium

6. **#4 `n`** — "since his own men will never see the end of their wandering" is false (they reach Italy). Replaced by
   the neutral point that Aeneas looks past the voyage itself. Also "subject of the impersonal `iuvabit`" muddled
   an infinitive subject with an impersonal verb: now "the infinitive is itself the subject of `iuvabit`"; the
   note also now says `haec` is the object of `meminisse`; "the most quoted line" softened.
7. **#5 `n`** — "the first time the goal of the voyage is named as `Latium`" is false (`Latio` is in I.6). Now: named
   by Aeneas himself as the goal.
8. **#9 `n`** — "`refert`… the speech is a reply to the men's silent despair". Nobody has spoken to him. `refert` here
   is just "says, utters". Fixed.
9. **#16 `n`** — "the word [`pius`] is used here again, as in the first part": the adjective does not occur earlier in
   Book I (source checked: only `pietate`, I.10 and 151). Now says so.
10. **#16 `n`** — "all of these men, apart from Orontes, will turn up alive" overclaims (not checkable here). Now: Orontes was
    last seen going down with his ship (I.113–117, checked in the source); the others are unaccounted for.
11. **#17 `n`** — `velivolum` "of Virgil's own making" is not verifiable from the sources; now "a compound in the
    manner of Greek epithets". The stray "the first of the scene's changes" deleted.
12. **#19 `n`** — the gloss of `ob` ("what they are barred from because of the goddess's anger") says the opposite of
    the Latin; now "on account of… for Italy's sake".
13. **#25 `n`** — "he named the people `Veneti` (Patavium's earlier name)": not in the Latin and false as stated.
    Removed; the note says Virgil does not say which name.
14. **#27 `n`** — "Aeneas is Jupiter's grandson… `nos`": the Trojans (`nos`) are Jupiter's own stock through Dardanus,
    Aeneas his grandson through Venus; and `arx` "for the Romans' future deification" confused Aeneas with the
    Romans. Both fixed.
15. **#30 `n`** — "the look that Neptune used on the winds… in the simile of the statesman": the simile is of a
    statesman quieting a mob and nothing there is a look. Now a plain cross-reference to Neptune's calming of the
    sea in the previous part.
16. **#36 `n`** — `viderit` called "future perfect". The `-erit/-erint` forms are ambiguous; with `dum` "until" the
    sense is the perfect subjunctive of expectation. Note says so.
17. **#39 `n`** — "(a legend of the foundation)" for Romulus in the wolf's hide: unverifiable; now just describes
    the picture.
18. **#42 `n`** — "Juno is harsh, as in the opening lines": `aspera` is not in the opening lines; the poem calls her
    `saeva` from line 4. Fixed.
19. **`about`** — "the council of the gods that follows": there is no council, only Jupiter and Venus; and the Caesar
    does not himself close the gates (the gates are shut by Faith, Vesta and the brothers' age of peace). Rewritten.
20–25. **Strong echoes of a known version, rephrased:** #14 `i` (nearly Fairclough's "stretched along the grass, fill
    themselves with old wine and fat venison"); #30 `i` ("with the look that clears sky and storm… lips"); #35 `i`
    ("since this care gnaws at you"); #37 `i` ("thirty great circles of rolling months"); #50 `i` ("closed with iron and
    close-fitting bars", also not what `compagibus` means: joints); #51 `i` ("his hands bound behind… hundred brazen
    knots").

## Low

26. **#9 `l`** — "he presses deep in his heart the grief" let `altum` read as an adverb; now "he presses the deep grief in his heart".
27. **#16 `n`** — `Oronti` gloss tightened (an `-i` genitive like `Achilli`).
28. **#17 `n`** — label tidied: "`iacentis`, `populos`" → "`iacentis` agreeing with `terras`".
29. **#17 `l`/`i`** — "sail-winged sea" is the stock rendering of `velivolum`; now "sail-flying" (the note's own gloss) and "the sea where sails go flying".
30. **#15 `i`** — "the last extremity… deaf now to any call" echoed a known version; rephrased.
31. **#19 `i`** — "govern the affairs of men and gods by eternal decree… what offence so great could my Aeneas commit" rephrased.
32. **#23 `n`** — clumsy last sentence ("the god Aeneas had in mind for the answer") recast (pass 2).
33. **#27 `i`** — "betrayed… far from the shores of Italy" echoed; rephrased.
34. **#29 `i`** — "Is this how you restore us to the throne?" → "Is this how you set us back on the throne?"
35. **#33 `i`** — "great-hearted… you will see the city and the promised walls" rephrased.
36. **#41 `i`** — "dominion without end" is a stock phrase; now "I have granted them rule that knows no end." `n`: "most quoted" → "one of the best-known".
37. **#42 `i`** — "with her dread" (whose dread?) → "with terror".
38. **#44 `i`** — "bring… under servitude / lordship over conquered Argos" rephrased.
39. **#45 `i`** — "to bound" read as purpose; now "one who will bound".
40. **#51 `n`** — "the poem's largest single statement of its theme" overclaims; now "one of the fullest statements of Rome's destiny".

## Scansion (hand scansion of all 99 lines)

Every long syllable was classed as long by nature or by position and every short checked; the scanner is
unreliable on exactly the cases the runbook names, plus several the runbook does not. **Ten lines added to
`scan-fixes.json`** (each with its reason there):

| line | what was wrong |
|---|---|
| 1.213 | `aena` is a-ē-na (trisyllabic, as `aenis` at 295), `litore` elides into it; scanner read `ae` as a diphthong and made `to` long |
| 1.220 | initial `Ae-` (Aeneas) split |
| 1.231 | initial `Ae-` split |
| 1.232 | `Troes` is two syllables (Trō-ĕs) and `potuere` has short `po-`; scanner had `Troes` as one syllable and `po-` long |
| 1.249 | `Troia` (neuter plural) is three syllables, short final `-a`, as 1.119 |
| 1.252 | `disiungimur`: consonantal `i` after the prefix (dis-iun-gi-mur) |
| 1.257 | `Cytherea` is four syllables (rē long) and `manent` has short `ma-`; scanner had `rea` as one and `ma-` long |
| 1.260 | initial `Ae-` (Aenean) split |
| 1.284 | `Assaraci` has short `sa`, `ra`; `Phthiam` is two syllables (Phthī-am); scanner had the reverse |
| 1.290 | `secura` has long `se-`/`cu-` and short final `-a`; scanner had `se-` short and a long `ra`, and `vo-` long |

**The three lines the packet flags were scanned by hand and the scanner's fit is correct**, so they are not in
`scan-fixes.json` (the COSTLY report for them is expected at build):
- **1.251** *nāvĭbŭs īnfān(dum) āmīssīs ūnīŭs ŏb īrăm*: `āmitto` has long ā (ab + mitto); `dum` elides into it;
  `unius` needs its ī lengthened (ūnīus), the only fit. Hiatus at the parenthesis not needed (elision is regular).
- **1.267** *āt pŭĕr Āscănĭŭs, cuī nunc cōgnōmen Īūlō*: `cui` monosyllabic and long, `Ascanius` four syllables, `Iulo` Iū-lo.
- **1.288** *Īūlĭŭs ā māgnō dēmīssum nōmen Īūlō*: `Iulius` three syllables, `a` long (ā), `sum` long by position before `no-`.

Other readings accepted from the scanner after test (kept, not in `scan-fixes.json`): 1.199 `dabit` with `-bit`
lengthened at the caesura and `deus` disyllabic; 1.220 `praecipue` with the final `e` long in arsis; 1.219 `iam`
elided before `exaudire` (so `nec` long); 1.223 `aethere`; 1.229 `deum` disyllabic; 1.231 `meus` disyllabic; 1.250 `tua`
disyllabic; 1.256 `dehinc` monosyllabic; 1.258 and 1.270 `Lavini` with short `La-` (the only fit at both places); 1.266
`transierint` with vowel `i`; 1.287 `Oceano` (ō-ce-a-no); 1.295 `aenis` trisyllabic (ă-ē-nis), the reading now also applied to
`aena` at 213.
Lines with Eu-: none besides Teucri (235, 248: correct as diphthong). Hiatus: none in the part.

## Refused / verified and kept

1. **I.203 `i`** "Perhaps there will come a day when we are glad to call even this to mind." Checked against every
   remembered version of this line ("one day it will be a joy to remember even this" and its family): it shares
   only the content word "even this"; kept. Only `l` changed (number of `haec`).
2. **#1 `i`** "worse than this": `graviora` has no stated comparand; "than this" is the natural supply. Kept.
3. **#0** `ante` as adverb, `ignari… malorum` genitive: verified true.
4. **#6 `n`** forward reference to Apollo at Delos (Book III): true; kept.
5. **#14 `n`** the wine given by Acestes (I.195, checked in the source): true.
6. **#17 `n`** "compare the opening of the Odyssey, and Iliad 24" for heaven-scenes: plausible, not checked here; kept.
7. **#20 `n`** `qui… tenerent` as purpose/characteristic (strictly also a relative clause in indirect speech): kept.
8. **#21–#22 `n`** `hoc` ablative, `actos` agreeing with `viros`: verified.
9. **#24 `n`** Antenor, Liburnians, Timavus: standard; kept.
10. **#38 `i`** "twin sons" for `geminam prolem`: the sex is the story's, not the Latin's; kept as natural.
11. **#43 `l`/`i`** "so it has been decided / resolved": kept (`placitum (est)`).
12. **#45** Julius / Iulus spelling difference between `l`/`i` (English "Julius") and the Latin name: left, conventional.
13. **#46 `i`** "no longer afraid" for `secura`: kept.
14. **#49 `n`** Quirinus as deified Romulus: true.
15. **#50 `n`** Janus gates shut 29 BC: true.
16. **#9 `n`** "a figure Virgil returns to": vague, harmless; kept.
17. **Speech marks**: Aeneas I.198–207, Venus I.229–253, Jupiter I.257–296 (closes at 296, inside this part); all open and close on the right units in `l` and `i`.
18. **Latin Library**: no variants in this stretch (packet says none).
19. **Echoes judged not distinctive** (kept): #0, #1, #5, #6, #7, #8, #20, #21, #23, #46–#49 `i`.
